messages:
incidents-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: KV_CACHE_OOM detected in hosted-runtime-us-west-2. Error rate spike, multiple customer errors 503. Triggered auto-pager.

maya_oncall: seeing lots of 503s and GPU OOMs on host-group rw-ht-*. Alerting here — taking lead. Anyone on-call for runtime?

raj_eng_runtime: i'm on it, will join. quick snapshot: memory for kv-cache per-host jumped from ~2GB to ~18GB in <2m. batch window ID 0x7fa3 grew key-count dramatically.

zoe_sre: impact: ~6% of production requests failing, higher on longer prompts. Affected customers: 3 Hosted API tenants observed degraded latency + failures. No dedicated customers.

anna_support: i already pinged CSMs for the 3 tenants; letting them know we're investigating. They reported a single customer sending very large uploads in a single prompt.

lee_devex: any clue on root trigger? recent rollout?

raj_eng_runtime: we pushed a prefetch heuristic change in canary 45m ago (reduce max-prefetch-length -> 65536 -> 131072) — appears to have a bug where extremely long single-utterance prompts skip the per-request cap and prefetch multiplies across continuous-batching windows. result: kv entries multiplied per-batch.

maya_oncall: plan: 1) throttle prefetch & continuous batching 2) fail fast on >1e6 tokens 3) route new wide prompts to fallback model variant. want to patch flags now.

ops-bot: NOTE: runbook step 1 initiated by maya_oncall at 1962500035

raj_eng_runtime: taking hotfix. toggling feature flags: set PREFETCH_ENABLED=false for hosted-runtime-prod, reduce CONT_BATCH_MAX_WINDOW=1, enable STRICT_PROMPT_LIMIT. running commands now:

```
# disable prefetch
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" https://controlplane.redwood/v1/flags/prefetch -d '{"enabled":false, "env":"hosted-runtime-prod"}'

# shrink continuous batching window
curl -X POST https://controlplane.redwood/v1/flags/cont_batch -d '{"max_window":1}'

# set strict prompt token cap
curl -X POST https://controlplane.redwood/v1/flags/strict_prompt -d '{"cap_tokens":500000}'
```

raj_eng_runtime: commands applied. verifying hosts...

zoe_sre: noticing drop in kv-cache allocation on rw-ht-01 within 30s. OOMs stopped on that host. overall 503s falling from 6% -> 1.2% in last 2m.

maya_oncall: good. let's keep prefetch off until we have a safe cap fix. raj, can you instrument a per-request kv-accounting metric? we need to track multiplicative factor across batching windows.

raj_eng_runtime: yes adding metric: runtime.kv.prefetch.multiplicative_factor and runtime.kv.per_request_keys. will push in a minor release to canary then prod. timeframe ~30m.

lee_devex: we should also add a temporary customer-facing limit and clearer error message for oversized prompts, so they don't retry aggressively. anna, can you prepare a blurb for support?

anna_support: on it. draft: "We're investigating intermittent 503s caused by excessive long single prompts. We've deployed a temporary protection that may reject very large inputs with HTTP 413. We're working on a permanent fix." will share with CSMs now.

emily_prod: need customer impact summary for execs: affected tenants, start/end times, root cause summary, mitigation, follow-ups. maya/raj can you provide?

maya_oncall: incident timeline: 1962500000 alert trig -> 1962500035 hot flags toggled -> 1962500100 OOM observed on two hosts -> 1962500135 mitigation effective -> 1962500180 stabilization. estimate customer impact window ~3.5 minutes.

raj_eng_runtime: root cause: prefetch heuristic regression allowed uncapped prefetch multiplication when continuous batching merged requests that contained giant single prompts. reproduction steps captured.

zoe_sre: post-mortem action items (short):
- revert/patch prefetch heuristic to enforce per-request cap (owner: raj, ETA: 24h)
- add multiplicative_factor metric and dashboard (owner: raj, ETA: 6h)
- add emergency feature flag to disable prefetch per-customer (owner: maya/ops, ETA: 3h)
- implement 413 with clear error and retry guidance (owner: anna/devex, ETA: 12h)
- run load/regression tests with synthetic long prompts (owner: eng-sre, ETA: 48h)

maya_oncall: for on-call handoff: i'll leave notes and hand to zoe in 20m. ops-bot i'll mark stable in 15m.

ops-bot: RUNBOOK UPDATE: incident marked stabilizing by maya_oncall at 1962500170. Scheduled postmortem and follow-ups created.

anna_support: CSMs notified; customers received preliminary status update. one tenant asked for logs, i'll coordinate with raj for sanitized traces.

emily_prod: thanks — include the mitigation commands and timeline in the exec summary. also highlight that Dedicated and Private weren't impacted — good to note.

raj_eng_runtime: pushing a small-scope fix to prefetch that reintroduces strict per-request cap and a hard upper bound on aggregated keys. will do canary in 1h.

zoe_sre: handing over monitoring to eng-sre. maya, leave anything else in the incident doc?

maya_oncall: added notes: see attached quick logs and the failing request sample (redacted). handover at 1962500185.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: KV_CACHE_OOM (stabilized). Final status: temporary flags applied, customer updates sent, follow-ups scheduled.

anna_support: closing thread for now, will reopen if regressions reappear.
